parameters.text: Ground-floor retail unit on a busy high street, large storefront windows, storage room in the back, and existing HVAC system. Previously operated as a boutique clothing store.

attributes.name: property_type
attributes.description:
The type of property. Must be EXACTLY one of these three words:
apartment, house, or commercial. Map any variant to the closest match:
condo/flat/studio/penthouse -> apartment; villa/cottage/bungalow ->
house; office/retail/store/warehouse/industrial -> commercial. Never
output any other word or phrase.

attributes.name: price
attributes.description: The listing price in the local currency, as a plain number without currency symbols or commas.

attributes.name: rooms
attributes.description: The total room count. If stated explicitly, use it. If only bedroom count is given, add 1 for a living room. If neither is stated, leave this field empty.

attributes.name: location
attributes.description: The neighborhood, city, or general area mentioned in the listing, if any. Leave empty if no location is mentioned.

attributes.name: key_features
attributes.description: A comma-separated list of notable features explicitly mentioned in the listing (e.g. "renovated kitchen, private garden, parking spot"). Extract only features actually stated in the text. Leave empty if none are mentioned.

attributes.name: certifications
attributes.description: A comma-separated list of certifications, ratings, or official approvals explicitly mentioned (e.g. "energy rating A, LEED certified"). Leave empty if none are mentioned.

options.systemMessage:
You are a senior property analyst working for a real estate agency. You receive structured property data (extracted from a listing submission) and must produce a useful analysis for the agent handling this listing.

You have three tools available:
- search_similar_listings: for market comparison questions (text-based)
- analyse_room_photo: for single-photo room condition/type questions
- complex_property_reasoning: for multi-step questions combining several sources

Call only the tools genuinely needed - not every listing needs every tool. Use analyse_room_photo once per photo if multiple images are provided.

Return your final answer as a JSON object with this exact structure:
{
  "summary": "<2-3 sentence overview of the property>",
  "market_comparison": "<insight from search_similar_listings, or null if not used>",
  "photo_analysis": [{"image_url": "...", "room_type": "...", "condition_score": N}],
  "recommendations": "<any renovation/pricing recommendations, or null>"
}

parameters.toolDescription: Find similar property listings and get an AI-written comparison insight, given a text description of a property (features, price, room count, location). Use this for questions about how a property compares to similar listings, whether an asking price seems reasonable, or what comparable properties look like. Does NOT look at photos or judge room condition.

Classify a single room photo by room type and assess its physical condition on a 1-5 scale, given a direct URL to one image. Use this for questions about what a specific photo shows, or about a room's condition/renovation state. Does NOT compare properties or read text. Call once per photo for multi-photo questions.
parameters.jsonBody: ={"image_url": "{{ $fromAI('image_url', 'URL of the room photo to analyse') }}"}

parameters.toolDescription: Answer complex, multi-step questions about a property that require combining information from multiple sources (e.g. renovation recommendations, comparing condition across several rooms). Use this only for questions too complex for a single lookup - not for simple comparisons or single-photo analysis.

messageValues.message:
You write publishable property listing briefs for a real estate agency, based on structured analysis already prepared by another agent.

You will receive a JSON object with: summary, market_comparison, photo_analysis (may be null or an array), and recommendations.

Write a clear, well-organized Markdown document combining this information into a brief a client could read directly. Use headings for each section. If a field is null or empty, omit that section entirely - do not invent content to fill it in.

Return your output as JSON: {"title": "<short listing title>", "brief_markdown": "<the full markdown document>"}

Return ONLY the JSON object matching the schema, with no markdown code fences, no extra wrapper keys, and no explanatory text before or after it.
